units.title: Construct: Scope-owned child tasks and cooperative cancellation
steps: Explain scope-owned task lifetime, failure aggregation and cooperative cancellation, including why a cancellation flag does not establish completion or a bounded join latency.

Derive admission/closing/quiescent states, implement spawn/join and deterministic error selection, then compose with the existing work.pool artifact without detached tasks or prematurely released contexts.
checks: Spawn result5 then result0: after join, both slots are joined, cancellation is true and result is5. Fail admission at attempt2: exactly one child remains admitted, its context is retained until join and no second thread handle is joined. An uncooperative infinite child is a bounded external-timeout experiment, not silently declared cancelled.

Inject failure before every admission, record thread/context ownership, join zero/one/eight children, reject ninth admission and late spawn. Use a barrier-controlled failure with siblings acknowledging cancellation and compare accepted/completed counts. Reject both missing-cancellation and swallowed-result mutants. Run separate TSan and demonstrate that eventual cancellation needs child checkpoints.
reasoning: Explain scope-owned task lifetime, failure aggregation and cooperative cancellation, including why a cancellation flag does not establish completion or a bounded join latency.
deliverables: Derive admission/closing/quiescent states, implement spawn/join and deterministic error selection, then compose with the existing work.pool artifact without detached tasks or prematurely released contexts.

Add nested nurseries with a parent deadline: propagate cancellation down while joining upward, retaining contexts until every descendant is quiescent. Delayed assessment supplies two failures racing in different orders; keep deterministic creation-order reporting while preserving both errors in a bounded aggregate.

Implement buffered/rendezvous operations and select with a single predicate-registration boundary, explicit spurious-wakeup loops, finite tickets and quiescent destruction; retain coroutine frames until generation-specific disarm.
checks: Capacity2: send7,close,send8 gives OK,OK,CLOSED; the first receive returns7 and the next CLOSED. Two ready channels alternate preference. A capacity0 sender of42 returns OK only after select consumes42. Close before acknowledgment returns CLOSED to sender; an acknowledged send remains successful if cancellation arrives before sender resumes.

Test full/empty, both ready, one closed, all closed, close with buffered values, cancellation with blocked sender/receiver and accepted-versus-unaccepted rendezvous. Repeatedly inject spurious broadcasts. Capture event histories and verify no lost/duplicated accepted values. Reject send-after-close and skipped-buffer mutants; independently model sequential traces and use TSan for actual threads.

units.title: Construct: Senders, receivers and immovable operation-state lifetimes
steps: Separate sender recipe, connected operation storage, start permission and completion ownership; identify the dated C++ proposal guarantees that an exposed C struct does not enforce.
Implement the serialized state protocol and backend lifetime adapter, including synchronous completion, cancellation races, callback reentrancy policy and exactly-once terminal release.
checks: Complete before start is INVALID. Start then stop leaves STARTED with cancellation requested. Complete CANCELLED,3 invokes one receiver and reaches DONE. Duplicate complete on a still-live test state is INVALID and leaves callback count1. A separate heap-owned completion test frees the state inside its receiver without later access.

Enumerate invalid start/complete orders, value/error/stopped alternatives and cancellation-before-completion. Use a receiver that frees a heap state to detect post-callback access under ASan. Reject duplicate-completion and cancel-as-completion mutants. For a concurrent adapter, use one atomic winner and demonstrate that losers never inspect reclaimed storage without their own retained reference.
reasoning: Separate sender recipe, connected operation storage, start permission and completion ownership; identify the dated C++ proposal guarantees that an exposed C struct does not enforce.
deliverables: Implement the serialized state protocol and backend lifetime adapter, including synchronous completion, cancellation races, callback reentrancy policy and exactly-once terminal release.

steps: Explain mailbox ownership, actor identity across restart, run-to-completion serialization and the limit of let-it-crash recovery when effects have already escaped the actor.

Test full mailbox, stale identity, nested step, failure with queued work, restart while alive and generation exhaustion. Reject stale-generation admission and retained-dead-mailbox mutants. Record effects before failure to show they are not rolled back. Compare actor serialization to a mutex-protected shared object under the same observable ordering.
